div.head: II Eg 4
div.ab: ⁊ sy ælc heorðpæning agyfen be Petres mæssedæg.
⁊ sy ælc heorþpening agyfen be Petres mæssedæg.
Et omnis heorðpeni reddatur ad festum sancti Petri.
[Be þon heorþpeninge.] [Ld] ⁊ sy ælc heorðpænig agifen be Petres mæssedæg.
And every hearth-penny shall be paid by St. Peter's Day.
And every hearth-penny is to be paid by St Peter’s day.
(Von dem Herdpfennig. Ld) Und jeder Herdpfennig werde zu Petri Festtag [1. August] abgeliefert.
(Of the hearth-penny. Ld) And let every hearth-penny be paid by St Peter's day [1 August].
div.note: Co has ‘Rompeni’ and ‘Vincula’ in the lower margin of the Latin.
A penny from every house, by this time identical with Peter’s Pence.
Probably the feast of St Peter and St Paul, 29 June; see p. 444, n. 4.
